claims.text: High-pressure torsion processing can improve the hardness of high-entropy alloys.
High-pressure torsion processing can improve the strength of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed HPT treatment can improve hardness and strength without sacrificing useful mechanical performance.
HPT introduces lattice distortion into high-entropy alloys.
HPT refines the grains of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed treatment should operate at room temperature.
The proposed HPT treatment should use an applied pressure of 5 GPa.
The proposed HPT treatment should use five turns of torsion.
Grain refinement acts as a barrier to dislocation movement.
Lattice distortion acts as a barrier to dislocation movement.
Impeded dislocation movement enhances alloy strength and hardness.
HPT will increase Vickers hardness by at least 20% relative to an untreated as-cast or conventionally processed baseline.
HPT will increase yield strength by at least 15% relative to an untreated as-cast or conventionally processed baseline.
The mechanical-property improvement will be greatest in alloys that attain a high degree of lattice distortion and grain refinement during HPT.
The optimal lattice distortion and HPT conditions for maximizing improvement without sacrificing ductility are unknown.
The hypothesis is falsified if HPT produces less than a 10% increase in hardness or strength, or more than a 20% reduction in tensile ductility.

contradictions.description: The headline hypothesis states that useful mechanical performance will not be sacrificed, while the uncertainty field says that conditions achieving improvement without sacrificing ductility remain unknown.

The predicted improvements are at least 20% in hardness and 15% in yield strength, but the hypothesis is falsified only below a 10% improvement. Results between these thresholds would fail the prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
